question: Which of the following is the time period of the First Five year Plan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1951-1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• First Plan (1951-1956)

 
 
• The First Five-year Plan was launched in 1951 which mainly focused on the development of the primary sector.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Harrod–Domar model with few modifications.
 
• This then-president was **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** and Gulzarilal Nanda was the vice-president.
 
• It mainly addressed the agrarian sector, including investment in large dams and irrigation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Five-Year Plans

 
 
• These are national economic programmes that are controlled and integrated.
 
• In 1928, Joseph Stalin implemented the Soviet Union’s first Five-Year Plan.
 
• Most communist countries and a few capitalist ones have since adopted them.
 
• Various Industrialists in 1944 drafted a joint proposal for setting up a planned economy in India (Bombay Plan).
 
• Under the socialist influence of prime minister Nehru, India established its First FYP in 1951, shortly after independence.
